 O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Foden start as City make three changes 
 David Clayton 
 @dclayton_MCFC 
 Sat 21 Nov 2026, 11:15 
 Share 
 Ayyoub Bouaddi, Nico O’Reilly and Phil Foden all return to the starting line-up for City against Fulham for today’s lunchtime kick-off. 
 Making way are Enzo Fernández Rayan Cherki and Joško Gvardiol who all take a place on the bench.
 Abdukodir Khusanov has also recovered from the knock that kept him our of Uzbekistan’s recent internationals.
 Line-ups
 CITY: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, O’Reilly, Bouaddi, Anderson, Ndiaye, Foden, Doku, Haaland
 Subs: Rulli, Kovačić, Cherki, Fernández, Reis, Gvardiol, Allan, F. Samba, Lewis
 FULHAM:  Leno, Tete, Affengruber, Bassey (C), Sessegnon, Berge, Charles, Bobb, King, Iwobi, Muniz
 Subs: Kaiser, Castagne, Cuenca, Robinson, Larsson, Cairney, Angel, Palacios, Gonzalo
 Formation and tactics
 City will play our usual 4-3-3 formation this afternoon.
 Gianluigi Donnarumma will, of course, be in goal with full-backs O’Reilly and Khusanov on the left and right respectively.
 In central defence, Ruben Dias is partnered by Marc Guéhi -with the England defender recovering from the knock that kept him out of international duty.
 Protecting the back four will be Elliot Anderson and Bouaddi, who is joined in midfield by Foden who will have the chance to play in his preferred No.10 role.
 Our forward three will be wingers Iliman Ndiaye and Jérémy Doku on either flank, with Erling Haaland through the middle.
 Fulham are among the slowest build-up sides in the Premier League, with the majority of their attacks coming down the wings.
 Blues need three points
 Going into the international break, City suffered a demoralising 3-1 loss to Nottingham Forest.
 That meant a long fortnight of reflection for Enzo Maresca who, by his own volition, would have preferred to have had the opportunity for his team to respond straight away.
 It will be fascinating to see whether there any tactical tweaks against Fulham, though one aspect of our recent run of losses will be to try and eradicate the costly mistakes that have led to several opposition goals.
 But, as Maresca said at his Friday press conference, overall our record of 12 wins from 16 games is pretty impressive.
 And making 13 out of 17 will make everyone – manager, players and fans – feel a lot more positive again as the winter fixtures come thick and fast.
 Stats and facts
 City have won their last 17 Premier League games against Fulham, scoring at least twice each time. It’s the longest winning streak one team has had against another in English league history.
 City have won their last 20 games against Fulham in all competitions, the longest winning streak one team has had against another in English football.
 Fulham have conceded at least once in their last 32 Premier League games against  City (80 goals in total). Their last clean sheet came in their first visit to the Etihad Stadium in March 2004 with Edwin van der Sar in goal.
 Fulham are unbeaten in their last four Premier League games (W2 D2), and have lost just one of their last seven (W2 D4).
 There have been as many goals in their previous seven games (11 – F6 A5) as in their opening three fixtures of the campaign (F4 A7).
 City and Fulham are the top two in the Premier League this season for build-up attacks (50 and 48 respectively) and passes per sequence (4.9 and 4.6), while ranking 19th and 20th for direct speed (1.5 and 1.4 m/s).
 Just 24.2% of Fulham’s attacking touches in the Premier League this season have come through the middle third (38.2% left third and 37.6% right third); it’s the second-lowest proportion, behind Everton’s 23.6%.
 Only Erling Haaland (9), Evanilson (9), João Pedro (8), and Pascal Gross (8) have been involved in more Premier League goals this season than Man City’s Rayan Cherki (7 – 5 goals, 2 assists), while having the league’s highest differential (+3.1) between his goals and expected goals this term (1.9 xG).
 Despite not recording an assist in the Premier League this season, Fulham’s Alex Iwobi leads the competition for expected assists (2.95) and is only behind Pascal Gross (29) for chances created (24). He’s also second for defensive line-breaking passes (39), while only three players have more line-breaking passes leading to shots than his 20.
 BE AT CITY V NAPOLI!
 City will look to move a step closer to UEFA Champions League knockout qualification as we face Napoli – and you can be here to cheer on the Blues!
 Enzo Maresca’s men take on Massimiliano Allegri’s Serie A side on Tuesday 24 November with a 20:00 (UK) kick-off at the Etihad.
 It’s our fifth game in the League Phase following four wins and one defeat and those results have left us seventh in the League Phase with the top eight automatically qualifying for the Round of 16.
 Make sure you’re here to support Maresca’s men with tickets now on sale to any Cityzens with an account active before 27 August. It’s up to four tickets per Cityzen - three additional for members on the UEFA Cup Scheme.
 You can also make a special night of it with a hospitality experience under the Etihad lights - packages start from £110 per person, with places in City Hall, Crossbar and Zadie’s all available in the new Pep Guardiola Stand as well as 12-seater Platinum Boxes and places in the Asahi Superdry Tunnel Club Premier.
